findings.reason: §5 must extend the departure hold (or state why the existing round-trip rule cannot cover a wait that recovers after the settle window) instead of adding a parallel same-word test, or the two rules will disagree about a run that both hold.
findings.text: §5 proposes "the stream no longer carries a row whose pane word is the same on both sides and whose wait facts are unchanged", which is a second same-word suppression rule beside the row policy's existing round-trip memory: `RowPolicy._shown`/`_departures` (ticker.py:1268–1272, `_note_shown` :1335) already holds a departure and drops it when the run "returns to it inside the settle window, so the pane draws neither half", keyed by run id and seeded across reloads; the plan cites neither the memory nor its window, so the recorded pair (wait-aged 10:47:05Z → waiting 10:52:33Z, five minutes apart) is exactly the pair that escapes the existing hold and the new rule would be the second mechanism deciding the same question for the same run

findings.reason: a release decision taken outside the seat owner can disagree with the readers above about whether a foreign seat is live (they call it live when the lease holder is that host or the stream is fresh), so §9 must name `watch_unit.py`/`runs.py` as the seat owner and the fleet-record reader it extends, or the two judgements will conflict.
findings.text: §9 proposes that a producer whose host differs from the fleet record's node "releases its seat and exits", re-deriving a question the codebase already answers in three places: `watch_unit.live_foreign_seat`/`live_foreign_seat_host` (:143–148) already returns a live seat's foreign host from the seat record plus host lease plus stream freshness, `watch_unit._record_producer_running` (:97) already decides whether a foreign producer is alive by its stream, and `runs.watch_host_lease` (runs.py:2837)/`_seat_host_is_local` (:2773) already own the lease and the local/foreign comparison; the plan §9 also names the fleet record by path only, while its reader is owned by `dispatch_launch.py:2128` (`base / "fleet" / "record.json"`) and `fleet_supervisor.RECORD_NAME` (fleet_supervisor.py:108)

findings.reason: a worker sent to "the module named in the manifest" re-discovers the owner at implementation time, and the two paths §4 could pick (runs.py publishing vs recovery_watch.py composing) are exactly the fork the item exists to prevent.
findings.text: census of deferred owners, each stating that §4 also proposes a stamping rule on the transition producer while leaving the producer unnamed: (1) §4 "the producer module that composes transition events (named in the manifest)" — the composer is `runs._stream_transition` (runs.py:2222) and `runs._publish_watch_transitions` (runs.py:2343), with `recovery_watch.py:1878` composing the transition dict itself; (2) §9 "the producer seat module named in the manifest" — the owner is `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py` (1001 lines; `watch_host_lease` :33, `_record_producer_running` :97, `live_foreign_seat` :148); (3) §10 "the classification module that composes a wait's next action (named in the manifest)" — the text that must change is `recovery_classification.py:1000` ("the recovery sweep will resume run {run_id} when the condition…"), and §10's own hedge "when that module is recovery_classification.py" shows the owner is knowable; (4) §11 "committed under `scripts/`" — the census instruments already live under `scripts/census/` (`death_census.py`, `carryover_census.py`, `pace_replay.py`), each one subject per module with a co-located test; §11 does not name that home, and its report path (`docs/evidence/fragments/<slug>/census.html`) sits outside the evidence convention the repo states for a landed plan (`docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html`)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — every section extends one already-deep module (recovery_classification 1866 lines, recovery_liveness 1479, ticker 2604, obligations 1435, budget_lift 1406, lift_watch 414) and no section proposes a new wrapper family over them; the only new file is §11's census instrument plus its own test, one module hiding its own reclassification walk.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — four write paths leave the owner unnamed ("named in the manifest") although the owner is statically resolvable, and §5 puts a second suppression rule beside the row policy's existing one; the census is on the FINDING line below.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 2036, cli_options 402, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23; no section adds a CLI option, an MCP view or a refusal family, and §8, the one section that could have added surface, states in its own text that no parallel reader and no section adds a second kind, so the added family is nil and nothing needs retiring.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites most machinery by name and those files exist, but it omits the two owners its new rules sit directly beside: the row policy already holds a round-trip suppression (`ticker.RowPolicy._shown`/`_departures`, ticker.py:1268–1272) that §5's same-word rule duplicates, and the producer side already holds foreign-seat readers (`watch_unit.live_foreign_seat` watch_unit.py:148, `_seat_names_a_foreign_host` :60, `_record_producer_running` :97; `runs.watch_host_lease` runs.py:2837, `_seat_host_is_local` :2773) that §9 does not cite.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 and §3 say in their own text "extend that predicate, or the arm beside it / Extend that resolver rather than adding a parallel one", and §8 says "No parallel reader and no second kind" while extending `_queued_review_fields`; §6 names the existing stamping path rather than adding one.
